title: The Mosby Partition
logline: The time capsule Ted and Marshall sealed freshman year finally arrives from Wesleyan, and its contents prove their legendary 'best friends from minute one' story never happened. Barney runs a betting pool on the box, and Lily guesses every item with suspicious precision, because she knows exactly who invented Wesleyan's time capsule program.
coldOpen: Kids, for fifteen years, Uncle Marshall and I told everyone we were best friends from minute one. Then, in the fall of 2011, a box came in the mail from Connecticut.

couch.line: The minute-one story. Dad, you told it at my sixth birthday. To the clown.
And the clown wept, Penny. But minute one turned out to be more of an estimate.

scenes.summary: Marshall arrives cradling the Wesleyan time capsule. Ted and Marshall tell the legend of minute one (imagined cutaway), each in a version flattering to himself. Barney opens a betting pool on what in the box will kill the legend. Lily's guess is suspiciously exact. Button: she knows which side the wall locks from.

beats.line: That Thursday, Marshall got a package at work. He buckled it into the cab.
Ted. It came. Wesleyan Residential Life. Our time capsule!
Marshall, we said to open it when we're old and successful.
Ted, I found a gray hair on Tuesday. And it was not on my head.
And I have tenure. And a knee that predicts rain.
Best friends from minute one.
Oh no. They fist-bumped. That means the legend.
Drink fast. It's eleven minutes.
It's nine minutes, and it's the greatest friendship story ever told.
I love this story. I believe every single word of it.
Wesleyan, 1996. I walk into my dorm room. A young visionary, in a scarf.
In August.
Hello, friend. I'm Ted. Someday I'm going to change the skyline of the world.
I'm Marshall. And I'm going to save the world that skyline is on.
Then let's stay up all night and never stop talking about our dreams.
I have two older brothers, Ted. But I've never had a brother.
Change the skyline of the world. You said that. At eighteen. Out loud.
I was a very quotable eighteen.
You always skip the part where you got homesick and cried, and I held you.
That was allergies.
To Connecticut.
Nobody is best friends at minute one. At minute one, I'm still deciding if you're a wingman or a human shield.
Something in that box kills this legend. And I am taking bets.
Twenty bucks says there's a photo of Ted in a cape.
It was a cloak. And it was a phase.
It's in the box.
Twenty says a love poem. Written by Ted. Addressed to Ted.
That's ridiculous. It was addressed to Future Ted.
Lily? You lived across the hall. Place your bet.
Me? Gosh. A legal document, a drawing of a wall, and a slice of pepperoni pizza.
A wall.
I'm a very visual guesser.
Lilypad, why would anybody put pizza in a time capsule?
Exactly! Who would do that? Monsters.
Saturday, our place. We open it with the ceremony it deserves. I'll prepare some remarks.
Lily. Hypothetically. What kind of wall?
Plywood, with a door that only locks from Ted's side.
Is my guess.

scenes.summary: The opening ceremony. Out come Marshall's nine-count lawsuit against Ted, Ted's blueprint for a wall down the middle of their dorm room, and a fifteen-year-old slice of pepperoni. Lily wins the pool with a perfect trifecta. The legend dies, and Ted and Marshall realize their friendship has no origin story. Robin reveals Wesleyan never had a time capsule program. Lily cracks.

beats.line: That Saturday, the opening ceremony began with a few brief remarks.
And the very first time capsule, sealed in 1876, contained a pen, a photograph, and a—
Ted, it's been forty minutes. I'm old and successful now. Open the box.
To be opened when we're old and successful.
Well. You're old.
Item one. Lily, it's a legal document. My very first legal document!
Eriksen versus Mosby.
Count one. Defendant says I pronounce my own last name wrong.
beats.title: Eriksen v. Mosby: A Complaint in Nine Counts
lines: Count 1: Says I pronounce my own last name wrong
Count 2: Wears a cape to Economics
Count 3: Calls the bunk bed 'the sleeping loft'
Counts 6 to 9: Too painful to write down

beats.line: You sued me?
I drafted, Ted. I never filed. Legally, that's just a very angry diary.
Count two. Cape. Pay me.
Cloak!
The bet was a photo. The house does not pay out on hearsay.
Item two. My first architectural drawing. I describe it in every lecture I give.
A cathedral of glass and light, drawn by a boy who dared to dream.
The Mosby Partition. A wall down the middle of the room. Soundproofed against chewing.
beats.title: The Mosby Partition
lines: A wall. Down the middle of the room.
Door locks from my side only.

beats.line: Soundproofed against chewing?
You chewed soup, Marshall! I could hear you chewing soup!
Count four, Ted. You alphabetized my cereal.
You had them sorted by color. Like an animal!
A legal document and a wall. Lily, you are two for two.
Huh. Lucky me. Probably no pizza, though.
There's one more thing. Wrapped in foil.
It's a slice of pepperoni pizza.
Somebody is so going to eat that.
Nobody ate the pizza, Luke.
Lily Aldrin. A trifecta. Nobody guesses pepperoni.
I'm a very visual guesser!
Marshall. If we hated each other on day nine, when did we become friends?
I don't know. I really thought it was minute one.
Best friends from minute one?
You alphabetized my cereal, Ted.
Ted, your remarks were so long, I called Wesleyan. Twice.
They have never had a roommate time capsule program. Ever.
Lily. Who sent the box?
Fine! I made it up! The program, the box, the Unity Coordinator. All of it!
Lily, you were the Unity Coordinator?
I was the whole department.

scenes.summary: The real day nine. Ted and Marshall aren't speaking. Lily, from across the hall, invents a job, a program and a deadline, and hands them a box. At three in the morning, Marshall catches Ted turning the music up to cover his crying, the way he has every night. They save the last slice for future us and leave the lawsuit and the wall inside. Lily, listening at the door: nailed it.

beats.line: Wesleyan, September 1996. Day nine. Your Uncle Marshall and I had not spoken since day five.
Could you type quieter?
Could you chew quieter? You're eating soup. How is soup crunchy?
It's chunky soup, Ted. It's a meal you can drink.
And for the record, in the original Norwegian, your name is pronounced—
It's my name, Ted! I'm the one who has it!
Hi! Lily Aldrin, from across the hall. And from Residential Life. I'm the Unity Coordinator.
We have a Unity Coordinator?
Since about four o'clock today.
Every roommate pair seals a time capsule. Put in something that sums up your year so far.
Residential Life mails it back when you're old and successful.
How will they know when we're successful?
Oh, they'll know.
Ted. I'm gonna marry that girl.
We're not speaking, Marshall.
I know. I just had to tell somebody.
By three in the morning, the box held one lawsuit and one wall. And then I heard the sound I'd heard every night that week.
It's Thursday. Back home, it's meatloaf night.
You do that every night.
Do what?
Turn the music up when I cry. So the guys down the hall won't hear.
It's a very good album.
I'm homesick too, you know. I wear the cape so that here, at least I'm somebody.
Ted. You are definitely somebody. You're the cape guy.
Last slice. Split it?
Or we save it. For future us. When we're old and successful.
Should we take out the lawsuit and the wall?
Leave 'em. Future us should know where we started.
Future us is going to be so confused.
And so hungry.
Nailed it.

scenes.summary: Back in 2011. Marshall learns Ted covered for him every night; Lily explains she only gave them an excuse, and that she was playing a long game at eighteen. Barney salutes the play and pays her anyway. The legend is rewritten: best friends from day nine. Then Marshall eats the pizza. Future Ted: so every night, I turned the music up.

beats.line: You turned the music up. Every night.
It was Enya, Marshall. Nobody plays Enya that loud for fun.
And for the record? You were the one who cried.
That was allergies.
Lily, you heard all that?
Through the wall. Every night. You crying, and Ted turning it up so nobody else could hear.
You two didn't need a Unity Coordinator. You just needed an excuse.
And you kept the box for fifteen years?
In my closet. Then last month I drove to Middletown so the postmark would match.
That's four hours, round trip.
Ted got tenure. Marshall got a gray hair. A Unity Coordinator keeps her word.
Lilypad. You gave me my best friend.
I had to. I needed you happy and distracted until I was ready to date you.
Lily, you were eighteen.
I was playing a long game at eighteen.
A fake job. A fake program. A fake deadline. Lily, that's not a time capsule. That's a play.
The pot is yours. Sixty dollars.
Barney, she knew what was in the box!
Robin. She was the box.
I've designed buildings all over this city. That wall is still the best thing I never built.
It only locked from your side, Ted.
So. Not minute one.
Three in the morning, day nine.
Best friends from day nine!
Great. Now the story has a third act.
Ted. There's just one thing left to do.
Marshall, no.
Future us is hungry, Ted!
Kids, Uncle Marshall ate the pizza. He was sick for three days.
So every night, I turned the music up.
